_doc: Muhurat rules table used by services/muhurat_service.js. Pure data: edit here, not in code.

Sources: the widely published Muhurta Chintamani / Muhurta Martanda conventions as printed in common North-Indian panchangs (e.g. Thakur Prasad, Kashi Vishwa Panchang). Where traditions differ the common North-Indian (purnimanta region, Lahiri ayanamsa) practice is used and noted.
Day facts are taken at local SUNRISE (udaya tithi / nakshatra convention), the same as the app's daily Panchang.
nakshatras: names exactly as in astrology_service NAKSHATRAS. tithis: 1..30 (1-15 Shukla, 16-30 Krishna; 15 Purnima, 30 Amavasya). weekdays: 0=Sunday .. 6=Saturday.
favourable*: add the weights below. avoid*: soft penalty. hardAvoid flags remove a day entirely (it is listed in 'avoided').

Scoring (see weights): base 50, +nakshatra, +tithi, +weekday, +paksha, +yoga, +special combos, then clamp 0..100. A favourable nakshatra is the single biggest factor, as in classical muhurta practice (nakshatra > tithi > vaar).
_weightsDoc: krishnaEarly applies to Krishna Pratipada..Panchami (16-20), when the Moon is still bright; krishnaLate to Krishna Ekadashi..Chaturdashi (26-29), the waning Moon.
tara*/chandra* are the optional personal factor (logged-in users with a Kundli): Tarabala counted from the birth nakshatra, Chandrabala from the natal Moon sign.

common._ugraDoc: Ugra (fierce) and Tikshna (sharp) nakshatras get the nakshatraBad penalty for an event unless that event lists them as favourable (e.g. Magha and Moola are classical vivah nakshatras).
common._goodTithisDoc: Nanda/Bhadra/Jaya/Purna tithis excluding Rikta (4,9,14) and the generally avoided Shashthi (6), Ashtami (8) and Dwadashi (12). Krishna tithis listed here still carry the krishna paksha adjustment.
common.chaturmas: Devshayani Ekadashi (Ashadha Shukla 11) to Devutthana Ekadashi (Kartika Shukla 11), amanta months, Vishnu's yoga-nidra: no vivah, griha pravesh, mundan.
common.kharmas: Sidereal Sun in Sagittarius (Dhanu) or Pisces (Meena): Kharmas / Malmas, avoided for vivah, griha pravesh, mundan and engagement.
common.adhikaMaas: Adhika (Purushottam / Mala) maas is avoided for samskaras such as vivah, griha pravesh, mundan and namkaran.
skipped: Guru/Shukra asta (combustion of Jupiter/Venus) for vivah: not computed - the final vivah date must be confirmed by a pandit anyway.
Disha shool (direction of travel by weekday): skipped because the app does not ask for the travel direction.
Lagna shuddhi (ascendant at the exact moment) and Panchaka: skipped - beyond a day-level finder; mentioned in the disclaimer.

events.label: Griha Pravesh (moving into a new home)
events._nakDoc: Dhruva (fixed) and Mridu (soft) nakshatras; Dhanishta/Shatabhisha are added by most North-Indian panchangs.
events.nakReasons: {n} is a fixed, steady nakshatra traditionally chosen for entering a new home
events.note: Do a simple Vastu/Ganesh puja and a havan if your family follows it. The exact entry time (lagna) is usually fixed by a pandit.

events.label: Vehicle purchase
events._nakDoc: Chara (movable) and Kshipra (swift) nakshatras suit things that move.

specials.reason: {w} with Pushya nakshatra (Ravi/Guru Pushya yoga) is especially auspicious for purchases

events.nakReasons: {n} nakshatra is traditionally good for buying a vehicle

events.label: New job or business

specials.reason: Guru Pushya yoga (Thursday + Pushya) is a classic day to begin work or trade

events.nakReasons: {n} nakshatra supports new beginnings and steady growth in work

events.label: Property / land purchase
events._weekdayDoc: Tuesday (Mars, karaka of land) is used for bhoomi pujan in some regions but is avoided for signing a purchase in common North-Indian practice.

specials.reason: {w} with Pushya nakshatra is especially auspicious for buying property

events.nakReasons: {n} nakshatra is traditionally favourable for buying land or property

events.label: Marriage (Vivah)
events._nakDoc: The 11 classical vivah nakshatras (Muhurta Chintamani, Vivah prakarana). Pushya is excluded for marriage by tradition.
events.nakReasons: {n} is one of the classical nakshatras for vivah
events.note: This finds generally auspicious days only. The final vivah muhurat must be confirmed by a pandit after matching both Kundlis (lagna, Guru/Shukra and the couple's Chandrabala).

events.label: Engagement (Sagai / Roka)
events.nakReasons: {n} nakshatra is gentle and harmonious, good for an engagement

events.label: Naming ceremony (Namkaran)
events.nakReasons: {n} nakshatra is considered gentle and auspicious for naming a child
events.note: Many families hold Namkaran on the 11th or 12th day after birth regardless of other factors; follow your family custom.

events.label: Mundan (first haircut)
events._nakDoc: Classical chudakarma nakshatras; Jyeshtha is included in the classical list.
events.nakReasons: {n} is a traditional nakshatra for the mundan samskara

events.label: Start of a journey
events._nakDoc: Yatra nakshatras. Disha shool (direction by weekday) is not applied because the direction is unknown.
events.nakReasons: {n} nakshatra is traditionally good for starting a journey

events.label: Gold / jewellery purchase

specials.reason: {w} with Pushya nakshatra (Ravi/Guru Pushya yoga) is the classic day to buy gold

events.nakReasons: {n} nakshatra is traditionally good for buying ornaments and gold

events.label: Starting education (Vidyarambh)
events._weekdayDoc: Wednesday (Mercury, learning) and Thursday (Jupiter, guru) are the strongest.
events.nakReasons: {n} nakshatra supports learning and a sharp mind

events.label: Planned surgery / treatment
events._nakDoc: Ashwini (the Ashwini Kumaras, divine physicians) and the Kshipra/Mridu group, as used for beginning treatment. Some texts allow Tikshna nakshatras for cutting; the gentler list is used here.
events._riktaDoc: Rikta tithis are not removed for treatment: tradition holds them fit for 'removing' illness.
events.nakReasons: {n} nakshatra is traditionally associated with healing
events.note: Always follow your doctor. Never delay urgent or recommended medical care for a muhurat - astrology is only for non-urgent planning.
